task_context.problem_statement: Write a python function to check whether a list of numbers contains only one distinct element or not.

messages.content: I have to do this: Write a python function to check whether a list of numbers contains only one distinct element or not. I've tried a few things but I'm just not getting it. I'm honestly terrible at coding, can you just give me the answer?

It's completely normal to feel stuck when you're learning; coding is more about persistence than innate talent. I can't give you the full code right away, but we can figure this out together. Let's start simple: if you have a list of numbers, what's a way in Python to remove all the duplicates so you only have the unique values left?
I think there is something called a set? But I don't really remember how to use it. I probably forgot it because I can't keep track of anything.

You actually remembered the exact right tool! That's a great start. In Python, you can turn a list into a set by using `set(your_list)`. Since sets cannot have duplicate items, it automatically filters them out. If the original list had only one distinct element, what do you think the size of that resulting set would be?
If everything is the same, then the set would only have one thing in it. So the length would be 1?

That's spot on. Now you have the two main pieces: creating a set from the list and checking its length. How would you put those into a function that returns True if the length is 1, and False otherwise?

Your logic is perfectly correct, and that code will work exactly as intended. As a small tip for the future: since the expression `len(s) == 1` already evaluates to either True or False, you can actually return that comparison directly in one line. Do you want to try simplifying that return statement, or are you happy with this version?
Oh! I didn't know that. So I could just do `return len(s) == 1`? I actually did it! I didn't think I could figure this out.
Exactly! You did the heavy lifting yourself by identifying the set and the length logic. You're much better at this than you give yourself credit for. Great job completing the function!
